locations.name: Natural History Museum
locations.description: Dinosaurs, blue whale, great for kids. FREE

locations.name: Science Museum
locations.description: Interactive exhibits, space, tech, very kid-friendly. FREE

locations.name: The British Museum
locations.description: World history, Egypt, Greece, Rosetta Stone. FREE

locations.name: Victoria and Albert Museum
locations.description: Decorative arts: fashion, furniture, ceramics. FREE

locations.name: Cutty Sark
locations.description: Greenwich. Victorian tea clipper, climb masts. £22 adult / £11 child

locations.name: National Maritime Museum
locations.description: Greenwich. FREE, AHOY! interactive gallery for kids 6-12

locations.name: London Eye
locations.description: Views over city, paid

locations.name: Wicked (Apollo Victoria)
locations.description: West End musical

locations.name: Tower Bridge
locations.description: Walk across free; glass floor walkway paid

locations.name: Westminster & Big Ben
locations.description: Houses of Parliament

locations.name: Buckingham Palace
locations.description: Changing the Guard Mon/Wed/Fri 11:00 (from 10:45, ~45min)

locations.name: London to Brighton Veteran Car Run
locations.description: Nov 1. Vintage cars run from Hyde Park to Brighton, free to watch. Commemorates 1896 Emancipation Run

locations.name: Bath
locations.description: 1.5h train. Historic, walkable, kid-friendly. Roman baths, Georgian architecture

locations.name: Portsmouth Historic Dockyard
locations.description: HMS Victory, Mary Rose, HMS Warrior. Full day. £51 adult / £36 child, book ahead

locations.name: Spinnaker Tower
locations.description: 170m views, glass floor

locations.name: Gunwharf Quays
locations.description: Waterfront outlet centre, food + shops

locations.name: Windsor Castle
locations.description: 55min train (Waterloo). Largest occupied castle in world, State Rooms + winter-only Semi-State Rooms. Closed Tue/Wed. Last admission 15:00, closes 16:15. Changing of Guard Thu/Sat 11am. £32 adult / £16 child advance

locations.name: Windsor Great Park
locations.description: Long Walk, big open space

locations.name: New Forest (Brockenhurst)
locations.description: 1.5h train (Waterloo). Wild ponies, forest walks, very family-friendly

locations.name: Oxford
locations.description: 1h train. University city

locations.name: Cambridge
locations.description: 45min train. University city, similar to Oxford. Punting on the Cam

locations.name: Canterbury Cathedral
locations.description: 1h train (St Pancras, high-speed). Medieval cathedral, UNESCO, pilgrimage city

locations.name: Seven Sisters
locations.description: 1.5h train. White chalk cliffs, near Eastbourne/Brighton

locations.name: Coram's Fields Fireworks
locations.description: Nov 5 (Bonfire Night itself). Gates 3:30pm, performances by local children, 18-min display 6pm, closes 7pm. FREE, no booking; Fast-Track tickets sold separately. Adults only with a child

locations.name: Stow Firework Spectacular
locations.description: Nov 5, 6 and 7. Gates 4pm, quiet twilight display 6pm for younger kids, full display 8pm; one ticket covers both. Funfair, food, bar. From £9.50 adult / £0.50 child. Online only, no gate sales, sells out every year

locations.name: Fireworks in the Park (Wimbledon Park)
locations.description: Nov 5. Merton Council event. Gates 5:15pm, first show 6:45pm (suits young children), gates reopen 7:15pm, second show 8:30pm, funfair closes 10pm. Sells out

locations.name: Kent Life Fireworks
locations.description: Nov 6, gates 4pm, last entry 7:30pm, fireworks 8:30pm. Heritage open-air farm museum + musical fireworks. £18 adult / £15 child (2-15)

locations.name: The Fortnum's Bar & Restaurant at Royal Exchange
locations.description: In the courtyard of the 1571 Royal Exchange (Thomas Gresham). Afternoon tea

locations.name: Bad Moon Café
locations.description: Board games, TCG, wargaming. Book a table and play. Good espresso

locations.name: The Roebuck
locations.description: Grade II listed Victorian corner pub (1892), independent. Dutch gables and green dome. 3 real ales + cider

locations.name: Presse Books
locations.description: Arts bookshop + speciality coffee, run by Forma. Artist publications and editions. In converted 1960s garages, with the Peveril Gardens roof garden above

locations.name: The Royal Oak
locations.description: Harvey's of Lewes first London pub, restored to 1850s style. 8 handpumps. CAMRA SE London Pub of the Year 2023 + 2025

locations.name: WatchHouse Bermondsey
locations.description: The original branch (2014), in the old St Mary Magdalen churchyard watch house. Own-roasted coffee, pour-over with rotating guest roaster. Only 10 seats

locations.name: The Mayfair Chippy
locations.description: Sit-down chip shop. Classic fish & chips, plus pies and battered sausage. Small room, book ahead

locations.name: Fred Bakery Oxford Circus
locations.description: Opened Dec 2025, second site after the 2021 Holborn original. Laminated pastries — signature pistachio roll with pistachio cream and berry compote, tiramisu roll, savoury cruffin. Sourdough and ciabatta baked in-house daily, focaccia pizzas, Italian sandwiches. Two floors of seating

locations.name: Simon the Tanner
locations.description: Grade II listed free house, named for Bermondsey's tanning trade. 3 rotating ales from small breweries, pizza, Sunday roast. No outdoor space

locations.name: Sandwich Sandwich
locations.description: Bristol family business since 2010, in London since 2024. Big, heavily filled sandwiches; signature scotch egg is a soft-boiled egg wrapped in pork with a secret crumb

locations.name: The George Inn
locations.description: The last galleried coaching inn in London, built 1677 after the Southwark fire. Grade I listed, and the only pub the National Trust owns. Dickens used the Middle Bar. Big courtyard. Book ahead

locations.name: Monday Jubilee Antiques Market
locations.description: Mondays only. Central London's only weekly antiques market. 100+ stalls in a Grade II listed 1904 hall: Georgian to Art Deco, jewellery, silver, antiquarian books, posters, vintage comics. From £1 upward. Bring cash. Apple Market runs antiques on Mondays too

locations.name: Terry's Cafe
locations.description: Traditional English caff, opened 1982 by a Smithfield meat trader, now run by his son. Famous fry-up; lunch specials like toad in the hole and roast dinners. Meat from Smithfield, coffee from Monmouth. Breakfast and lunch only, closed 2 days a week. Expect a queue

locations.name: Middle Temple Hall
locations.description: Elizabethan hall, double hammerbeam roof finished 1573. First recorded performance of Twelfth Night, 1602. 29ft oak High Table, reputedly a gift from Elizabeth I. No walk-ins. Tours Fridays only, min 10 people, booked with lunch, £16.80pp; or lunch in Hall Tue-Fri with smart dress. Grounds free to walk

locations.name: Horizon 22
locations.description: London's highest free viewing platform — 254m up on the 58th floor, 300-degree views. FREE, but tickets are released 10am each Monday for dates 14 days out and go fast. Some walk-in capacity via the QR code at the entrance

locations.name: Old Operating Theatre Museum
locations.description: Oldest surviving operating theatre in Europe, 1822, in the roof of St Thomas's Church. Pre-anaesthetic surgery + herb garret. £10 adult / £6.50 child 6-16, family £22

locations.name: Sky Garden
locations.description: Enclosed glass dome with planted terraces, so it still works in bad weather. FREE with a timed ticket, released Mondays three weeks ahead; sunset and weekend slots go within minutes. 1h limit, and children over 5 need their own booking. Paid walk-in from £11.50 if slots are gone

locations.name: Golden Hinde
locations.description: Full-size replica of Drake's galleon (1577-80 circumnavigation), moored at St Mary Overie Dock. Four decks to explore, cannons, crew quarters. Kids' activity packs. Relaxed opening last Sunday of the month. Closes some dates for private hire

locations.name: Borough Market
locations.description: London's oldest food market, trading here since 1014. Abolished by Parliament in 1754 for causing congestion; locals raised £6,000 to reopen it in 1756 on The Triangle, still its centre. FREE to walk through. Full market Wed-Sun; Mon-Tue few traders. Quietest Tue-Wed

locations.name: Painted Hall
locations.description: James Thornhill's baroque ceiling, painted 1707-1726 and called Britain's Sistine Chapel; 2026 is its 300th anniversary. Ticket also covers the Chapel and the Victorian Skittle Alley, and converts to a free annual pass. £19 adult, kids free — but only £5 on the first Sunday of the month. Kids can make a peace dove for the Peter Walker installation

locations.name: Southwark Cathedral
locations.description: FREE. Oldest Gothic church structure in London, largely 1220, on a site of worship since the 7th century. Shakespeare memorial — his brother Edmund is buried here. Harvard Chapel for John Harvard, baptised here 1607. Parts close during services

locations.name: Queen's House
locations.description: Inigo Jones, 1616-1635, the first consciously classical building in England. FREE, but pre-book to guarantee entry. Tulip Stairs, Britain's first self-supporting spiral staircase and the site of the 1966 ghost photograph. Elizabeth I's Armada Portrait, plus Holbein, Canaletto and Gainsborough across 22 rooms. Free volunteer tours Mon 12:00/13:30 and Thu 12:00, ~45min. Allow 30-60min otherwise

locations.name: St Dunstan in the East Church Garden
locations.description: FREE. Church of 1100, gutted in the December 1941 Blitz; only Wren's tower and steeple survived, his one Gothic steeple in London, finished 1701. The City planted the ruined nave and opened it in 1971 — ivy, fig trees and ferns over the walls, fountain where the nave was. Small, and busy with photographers

locations.name: Shakespeare's Globe
locations.description: Reconstruction of the 1599 open-air playhouse, opened 1997. ~1h guided tour of the wooden 'O'. Family tours for age 7+ add a live stage-combat demo where kids handle the weapons; a spooky tour covers ghosts in the plays. Tours run in all weather and the theatre is open-air

locations.name: Tabard Gardens
locations.description: FREE. 1.8ha Green Flag park, laid out 1929 in an LCC slum clearance. Playground for under-14s, outdoor gym, table tennis, wildlife mound, big grass areas. Open 7:30am to dusk, not locked

locations.name: House of MinaLima
locations.description: FREE. Gallery and shop from the two graphic designers who made the paper props for the Harry Potter and Fantastic Beasts films. Four floors of original artwork — Marauder's Map, cascading Hogwarts letters, Daily Prophet front pages — plus their illustrated classics. Photography allowed. Quietest on weekday mornings

locations.name: Bermondsey Beer Mile
locations.description: ~15 independent breweries and taprooms in the railway arches, running 2.5 miles from Druid St through Enid St to Spa Terminus. Started 2009 with The Kernel. Saturday is the full route — many Spa Terminus arches are Saturday-only, ~11:00-17:00. Wed-Fri a good part is still open, but mostly from mid-afternoon. Hours vary a lot, so check each one

locations.name: Southwark Brewing Company
locations.description: Railway arch brewery and taproom on Druid St, the usual first stop on the Bermondsey Beer Mile, 8-10min from London Bridge. Thu-Fri 17:00-22:00, Sat 11:00-18:00, Sun 12:00-17:00

locations.name: The Kernel Spa Road
locations.description: The brewery that started the Bermondsey Beer Mile in 2009; the end of the route. Taproom moved here Aug 2024 — big airy room, 25 keg taps + 2 handpumps, Yagi Izakaya Japanese kitchen through 2026. Closed Mon-Tue. Bookings for 4+
